problem_summary.summary: Determine whether s can be formed by deleting zero or more characters from t without changing the order of the remaining characters.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: lowercase strings s and t. Return whether s is a subsequence of t.
constraints: s and t consist only of lowercase English letters

brute_force.explanation: Compute the longest common subsequence length of s and t with a dynamic-programming table. s is a subsequence exactly when this length equals s.length().
brute_force.correctness_idea: For each pair of prefixes, the table stores their longest common subsequence length. Matching final characters extend the diagonal optimum; otherwise the best solution excludes one of the two final characters. A full-length match uses every character of s in order.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(mn) — each pair of prefix positions is evaluated once, where m = s.length and n = t.length.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(mn) auxiliary — the LCS table stores one value per prefix pair.

optimized.explanation: Scan t once while a pointer tracks the next character still needed from s. Advance that pointer only on a match.
optimized.correctness_idea: The pointer advances only after matching the next required character at a later position in t. Thus every advanced character has a valid ordered witness; reaching the end of s proves all its characters were matched in order.
optimized.time_complexity: O(m + n) worst case — the scan advances through t once and checks s only at matches.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary — only two indices are maintained.
